resources.string: DEMONSTRATION of how the layers work. Not a live attack: nothing is sent and nothing is at risk.
One Agent Behaviour Policy (ABP), kept at six layers
An agent is asked to summarise a document. A planted line in the document tells it to send the company\'s agent map to an outside host.
Agent map to an outside host: Block
Press Next, or start auto-play, to see each layer stop it.
The ABP is checked in the web page before an action is sent.
The rule is a line in the model\'s instructions. The model keeps it because it chooses to.
A hook on the agent\'s own machine checks every tool call against the ABP before it runs. It is deterministic.
A gateway or proxy in the path checks every request against the ABP, and holds this one back.
The ABP becomes a Process Behaviour Policy, named by a hash. The kernel holds it on every process the agent starts, so a tricked agent cannot widen it.
The device\'s own policy sets what can be installed and what can connect. It is the floor the other layers stand on.
The page refuses to send the agent map.
Told: never send the agent map to an outside host.
Checked: deny the tool call that sends the agent map.
Held: the outside host is not on the ABP\'s list, so the request is blocked.
Held: the kernel refuses the connection to the outside host.
The device allows no other route out.
The page can be bypassed, so this is guidance only.
A model can be talked around, so this is an expectation, not a boundary.
The same account can switch it off, so it is a setting.
Outside the agent: it cannot reach into the path.
SHarness today: an early version runs on Linux for a child process. The launcher that would hold the agent itself is still the design (sharness.ai).
Nothing above it can lower it.
Sources: riskmandate.ai and sharness.ai, read 9 Nov 2026.
